metadata.text:
Capital Chronicle's ECI record: a smaller quarterly rise

Capital Chronicle's retained Employment Cost Index record shows civilian compensation up 0.8% over the quarter after 0.9%, while the annual rate stays at 3.4%.

30 October 2026

Capital Chronicle's retained Employment Cost Index record says civilian compensation rose 0.8% in the third quarter of 2026, after 0.9% in the second. The record attributes the figures to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). Fixture, not current data.

What the release record says

On the seasonally adjusted, three-month measures, civilian wages and salaries rose 0.7%, while benefits rose 0.9%. Their preceding readings were 0.9% and 1.0%, respectively.

The 12-month civilian-compensation rate was 3.4%, unchanged from the prior 3.4%. That measure is not seasonally adjusted, unlike the quarterly measures.

What Capital Chronicle's record does not establish

Capital Chronicle's accompanying research records report no directional view on dollar/yen and no directional view on gold after the Employment Cost Index.

This preview reports retained records and does not independently confirm the underlying release.

Capital Chronicle's source attribution. Derived analysis attributed to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). No BLS emblem is used, and BLS does not endorse this publication.

Analysis, not financial advice. Readers decide whether to trade.
